title: docs(R9-C1): cut tests/README.md under its policy token cap
body:
Why this change, and what it measures.

The closures job's full arm — every push to main and the nightly — re-records
every selectable script through a hard-coded lane layout: `stress` alone,
`features`+`entities`, and everything else serially in one lane that takes
2,706 s of the job's 3,242 s recording wall (the round-9 closures pre-study,
2026-10-12, sections 1.2 and 2.4). The scoped arm has been lane-balanced by
`closure.py lane-plan` since R9-F10.15. This change gives the full arm the
same planner: with no `--single` and no `--scripts-from`, `derive_closures.sh`
derives its recording set from the tree (`lane-plan --all-scripts`: every
runnable test script but the SLOW_GATED ones — `merge`'s own expectation set,
the selectable scripts plus the driven children) and shards it with the same
planner at the CI bound of three lanes. Max recorded lane 2,706 s becomes
1,489.6 s (the replay script alone is the irreducible pole); CI wall est.
3,242 s becomes ~1,800 s on every push to main and the nightly.

The recordings' content is unchanged: same scripts, same per-script arguments
(`rec_special` carries golden.py's and env_drift.py's cheap arguments,
arch_score's `--smoke` and dst_checks' timezone on either path), the same loud
missing-recording check (now held against the planner's own `scripts.txt`
roster), the same `check --in-dir` under-approximation refusal, the same
upload; the full arm's local merge stays a full merge. Which lane records a
script changes WHEN it is recorded, never WHAT it opens — R9-F10.15, the
tree's own soundness argument — and the pre-study measured read sets
byte-identical under concurrency (its section 2.3); this seat re-ran one
parallel-vs-serial identity check of its own (under `## Figures`). The lane
layout becomes derived, not committed: the plan is computed at run time inside
the workflow's own step, so no numbers rot in the tree. A new selectable
script is recorded automatically, so the "add it to a lane on pain of a red
main" obligation disappears: ci_predict's NO RECORDING class is no longer
expressible (the arm returns nothing, documented where it stood), prepr 6d's
two planted NO RECORDING arms become null controls, and entities.py holds the
regrowth guard — any hard-coded `rec tests/...` line back in
derive_closures.sh reddens there.

The commission said this PR's CI would not exercise the full arm; it does.
The diff touches gate files (`tests/closure.py`, `tests/derive_closures.sh`),
so `closure-scope` derives the full case and this PR's own `closures` job runs
the balanced full arm on CI Linux — the pre-study's falsifying experiment
(recordings diffed against the committed table) runs itself here.

Review fix at the second commit: the entities regrowth guard's anchored
pattern (`^\s*rec tests/`) caught only 32 of the old layout's 34 rec lines —
`( rec tests/stress.py ) &` and
`HASTUB_TZ=Europe/Stockholm rec tests/dst_checks.py` escape it. The pattern
is word-boundary `\brec tests/`, and both escaping forms are planted arms in
the check: each must redden the anchored pattern and be refused by the guard
(they do, and it is; entities 2276/2276 green locally).

## Head

2268739c5

## Mutation proof

Planted in `tests/closure.py`, `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` run, then
reverted (both mutations red, restore green — `ALL 99 closure shrink pins
PASSED`):

- `i = 0` replacing `lane_plan`'s least-loaded-lane pick — every group into
  lane 1: `FAIL LPT balances the recorded seconds across the lanes [[220.0]]`
  and `FAIL the planned max lane is under half the table's recorded seconds
  [max 4014.7s, total 4014.7s]` (2 of 99 pins red).
- A planner that drops a script (the last entry of `scripts.txt` and of every
  lane file): `FAIL the CLI plans every input script over the live table`,
  and the runner refusal fired (`a script recorded by no lane fails the derive
  loudly` on the scoped shape).

## Null control

The unmodified layout over the same committed recorded-seconds table: lane 1
(stress) 760.6 s, lane 2 (features+entities) 548.1 s, lane 3 (everything
else, 31 scripts) 2,706.0 s — reproducing the pre-study's recorded 2,706.0 s
exactly. The balance pin's predicate `2*max < total` is False on that layout
and True on the planned one. Also: the first cut of the tests/README.md note
breached the file's own token cap (6,706 against 6,686) — cut in the second
commit, acceptance green again.

## Figures

- `python3 tests/closure.py lane-plan --all-scripts --lanes 3 --out-dir /tmp/c1-plan`
  — the full-arm plan at the CI bound: 3 lanes over 34 scripts, lane 1
  1489.6s recorded, lane 2 1262.6s, lane 3 1262.5s.
- `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` — prints the same three lane walls
  (`.. full-arm lane walls (recorded s)`) and holds the balance, coverage and
  edge pins over the live tree and table.
- `python3 tests/closure.py record tests/validate.py --out-dir D` (and
  `tests/wood_advisor.py`), serially and then with both recordings concurrent
  — `files` and `inert_reads` byte-identical serial vs parallel for both:
  validate.py 33 files, wood_advisor.py 85 files, rc 0 all four recordings.
  This is the pre-study's section 2.3 experiment re-run at this head.

## Red checks

`tests/entities.py` locally, first run: 47 checks of the a3-a13/hb fixture
families failed on this box, 46 of them identically on a pristine origin/main
checkout run as a control (main's or load-related, not this diff's); the 47th
was the policy-docs acceptance the README token cap above broke, fixed. The
full local re-run at the review-fix head — an otherwise idle box — passes all
2,276 checks, so those failures were contention, not the tree. Expected on
CI, not a defect: entities.py now reads `tests/derive_closures.sh`, so its
recorded closure grows and the closures job may print UNDER-SCOPED for it
once — `closures-autofix` re-records entities.py on Linux and merges the
widened entry, the designed repair. `tests.yml` is code-owned: the owner
reviews under the round-9 mandate after the push.

## Forward-carry

none

## Approval

The diff touches one measured-policy file: `tests/README.md` (a two-sentence
correction — the lane-entry obligation this change removes is stated there),
kept under its token cap. Per CLAUDE.md the owner approves a policy change
before it merges, not at drafting: this section is where that approval is
recorded. `tests.yml` is code-owned, so the same owner review covers the
mechanism; no `*_budgets.json` leaf is raised.

## Friction

none
